Catalogs capabilities, isolated commands, remaining production identity/storage/connection gates. Numerical historical test totals are dated evidence, not current acceptance.

Optional P2/P3 A2A-to-Relay composition: durable save/ACK remains SUBMITTED; explicit recipient acceptance and separately authorized Task submission precede execution. COMPLETED needs correlated durable result and independently verified closed engine evidence. Delivery runs through the Registry-guarded JetStream backend. That evidence-verified rule governs the preview composition with HabExecutionEvidence. A separate section records the owner's ADR-016 decision to wire the gateway into the host: off unless the config has an `a2a` section, a separate loopback listener, a host-owned Registry identity attested in-process as `urn:hab:host` with startup refusal codes, per-caller Registry checks of resolve/submit/execution_request with Tasks scoped per caller, private outbox/inbox/Task store, send only inside the owner's SendMessage with no background submit retry, a receiver loop that saves then ACKs only replies to host messages within one day of their request's expiry, ACKs any other or later delivery, and any reply under a new message ID that would not change its Task (previewed with held replies counted as confirmed), without an inbox or ACK record, applies each saved reply to its Task and releases the body once the Task is saved, releases unread a reply whose ACK can no longer be confirmed, fails a Task still without a result when the reply window closes (FAILED, reason result_window_expired, outcome unknown, a later reply changes nothing) in the receive cycle after the earliest open window closes, an ACK history counted per message, a blocking SendMessage that holds the Task serializer only per 25 ms check, an inbox of 2 × max_records reply bodies, outbox collection gated by actual inbox capacity after its minimum horizon, a host submit admitted inside the transaction that rechecks the caller, and reply-attested Task states labelled `attestation: "recipient_reply"` that claim no engine verification. Timeouts/cancel errors never claim stopped execution; no production/native-agent claim. The outbox horizon is only a minimum: inbox maintenance and a read-only whole-next-batch capacity gate precede outbox collection, preserving actual-local-terminal ACK retention after a long stop and deferring new admissions rather than accepting results that cannot fit. Window expiry is independent of the maintenance cadence; outbox body expiry still runs when row collection is deferred. This gate prevents future outbox collection; it does not restore source slots an earlier build already purged, repair already lost/quarantined results, or establish spare capacity in an existing deployment. Before resuming an affected deployment, quiesce new A2A admissions and let normal inbox maintenance and the full 30-day retention from actual local terminal time restore sufficient capacity. Do not delete history, shorten retention or re-execute Tasks with unknown outcomes. The whole-batch reserve may defer collection and admission longer than the minimum necessary. No live deployment has been checked. Task-store shutdown closes the eagerly opened SQLite connection even without SDK driver initialization, supports repeated close, and leaves saved state for reopening. requirements.title: Recipient-owned judgment
requirements.statement: HAB authenticates names, recipients, delivery and correlation; content understanding, refusal/questions/replies, task acceptance, execution and existing permissions/approval remain with the recipient agent. Do not centralize agent memories or judgment.
requirements.rationale: Preserves independent agents and prevents transport authorization becoming execution authority.
requirements.scope: All standard communication; recipient integration

requirements.title: Common product-independent messaging
requirements.statement: Standard connection uses shared HTTP MCP and durable inbox/outbox; recipient host periodically receives without a model. Do not add product-name delivery branches or a HAB product execution/approval runner as a prerequisite.
requirements.rationale: Native product capability/configuration differs, but delivery contract must remain reusable.
requirements.scope: Standard shared MCP and receive supervisor

requirements.title: Tasks are optional
requirements.statement: Ordinary question/answer communication works without creating Tasks. Existing fixed/generic Tasks, A2A and NATS execution ports are explicitly composed optional integrations; receive, ACK, listing or body reading must not automatically create task links, Tasks, model runs or replies.
requirements.rationale: Transport reception must not take or execute work on behalf of the recipient.
requirements.scope: Standard communication, including untrusted execution_request data

requirements.title: Durable receiver checkpoint before ACK
requirements.statement: Recipient deduplicates (sender_id,message_id), atomically stores message body and dedup plus durable original ACK request, and only then sends ACK; storage failure sends no ACK. Persist and reconcile the ACK receipt.
requirements.rationale: The Relay may delete body upon ACK; volatile conversation memory or direct poll-to-ACK is insufficient.
requirements.scope: Durable receive and standard/native MCP handoff

requirements.title: Durable sender identity and uncertainty
requirements.statement: Resolve recipient and commit immutable original envelope and selected sender/recipient IDs in outbox before submit; uncertain responses reconcile same message/content/deadline rather than new ID, new recipient resolution or later expiry.
requirements.rationale: Avoids duplicate delivery, silently rerouted requests and false nonexecution inference after lost responses.
requirements.scope: Sender outbox and resume/retry

requirements.title: ACK is receipt only
requirements.statement: Keep delivery, display/human-read, acceptance/execution/approval/completion as separate states. ACK proves durable receipt only; active registration is not online; timeout/cancel-request does not prove remote stop.
requirements.rationale: Every UI and evidence statement must match its observed state boundary.
requirements.scope: State APIs, UI, reports and recipient handoff

requirements.title: Pure source-authorized saved body read
requirements.statement: inbox_read requires independent exact-source authorization and current actor, pause/epoch, configured owner and idle checks, rechecks before returning authenticated unreleased saved body as an independent copy. Missing/released/corrupt data gives no body.
requirements.rationale: Metadata/receive permission must not silently grant body access; caller mutation must not corrupt saved evidence.
requirements.scope: Local AdapterHostCycle inbox_read

requirements.title: Read does not mutate receipt or act
requirements.statement: inbox_read may return saved receipt_confirmed=false data but must not retry/confirm ACK, release body, modify inbox/ACK/outbox/Task or initiate model/Task/reply. Existing reply/task acceptance guards stay unchanged; body is untrusted data, never direct owner approval.
requirements.rationale: Decouples pure retrieval from uncertain transport state and independent action authority.
requirements.scope: Local inbox_read and explicit recipient decisions

requirements.title: Receive-only supervisor authority
requirements.statement: Supervisor repeats receive only with same-agent durable stores, current authorization, process owner and explicit resume. It stops on missing/lost owner, pause or local authorization failure and never clears pause, obtains/releases owner, logs in, updates grants, sends replies, accepts tasks or starts a model. An optional owner-local authentication gate begins blocked after process start and may unblock receive only after fresh verified evidence of the exact approved issuer/resource/subject/client/connection/agent identity; it is not authentication or a replacement for current authorization. Copied, foreign, reused or superseded verification tickets cannot unblock it. Credential refresh/login, independent identity verification and native notification delivery remain product responsibilities.
requirements.rationale: A scheduler must not become privileged agent control or invent operational authorization.
requirements.scope: ReceiveSupervisor host port v1, optional trusted local recovery gate; synthetic recovery checks in test/authentication-recovery.test.js do not establish native OAuth or deployment acceptance.

requirements.title: Bounded receive and drain
requirements.statement: Configure finite receive interval/backoff/drain; only poll/ACK transport failures back off. A trusted local provider recovery signal becomes an explicit stop reason without a gate, or a blocked gate with bounded local-only waits and fixed, secret-free synchronous state notifications. Generic HTTP status or wire strings do not confer that local signal. No poll/ACK starts while blocked; current pause/owner/draining authority is rechecked before readmission. Storage failure stops without deleting data for room. Outstanding work prevents a new receive; stop prevents the next cycle and waits boundedly; drained=false does not certify safe DB/owner closure. Recovery retains original body/ACK and deferred send intent without extending existing time/attempt/retention horizons.
requirements.rationale: Avoids overlap, lost durable evidence and false cleanup success.
requirements.scope: ReceiveSupervisor timing, failures and cleanup

requirements.title: Current authorization and untrusted input
requirements.statement: Derive identity/operations/recipient from verified subject, client, scope and policy. Reject absent or failed authorization and recheck current authority at operation/commit boundaries. Agent names, message role, readonly prose, arbitrary headers or approval text confer no rights.
requirements.rationale: Prevents outside content or stale authorization from crossing into management/execution authority.
requirements.scope: All public entry points and recipient action integration

requirements.title: Group scope and address scope
requirements.statement: Approved authentication group may select its member addresses; deny outside-group names/mailbox operations and ambiguous selection. Same-group shared credentials do not prove exclusive per-Bot identity; sender/receiver IDs stay fixed across recovery.
requirements.rationale: Preserves adopted shared trust boundary without claiming isolation that shared credentials cannot provide.
requirements.scope: HAB authentication groups and five common MCP operations

requirements.title: Reusable inner Relay boundary
requirements.statement: Relay core/contract and durable client stay independent of HAB naming, registry, product/model SDKs, Task state, MCP SDK, OAuth and UI; outer composition injects narrow public ports. No hidden reverse dependency or import-time DB/listener/network effects.
requirements.rationale: Enables reuse and prevents standard messaging being coupled to execution or a vendor.
requirements.scope: Relay core/storage/client and composition boundaries

requirements.title: Idempotency and fenced receipt replay
requirements.statement: Same sender/message key and same content return original receipt/state without another message/delivery/task/notification; changed content conflicts. Atomic leases use generation/token; committed identical ACK receipt can replay after lease/TTL, while never-committed old ACK cannot steal current lease.
requirements.rationale: Lost responses and at-least-once delivery require durable identity rather than blind retry.
requirements.scope: Relay submit/poll/ACK/status

requirements.title: TTL retention and handoff
requirements.statement: Original message delivery TTL is one hour and never extends on retry/resume. Relay confirmed ACK atomically removes live message body and keeps minimum dedup/receipt for thirty days after max relevant horizon. Recipient body release requires explicit durable application handoff and does not follow delivery TTL automatically. Logical DB deletion is not all-copy physical erasure.
requirements.rationale: Limits retention without losing recovery/dedup proof or dropping recipient-owned content before handoff.
requirements.scope: Relay and client retention/GC

requirements.title: Pause and unresolved operations
requirements.statement: New host control begins paused; each command retains actor/epoch and rechecks before/after RPC and commit. Pause/local abort is not remote cancellation. Timeout retains busy/draining until underlying work settles; original ACK IDs/envelopes/task keys survive uncertainty.
requirements.rationale: Prevents stale late responses and overlapping work after a superficial timeout or pause/resume.
requirements.scope: Finite adapter host/control and optional task ports Managed transport is a trusted cooperative local-admission capability: unlike guarded fetch, its check releases the control transaction before physical SDK/IPC send. A request admitted before pause may still commit; every later request/retry needs a new current check. Product OAuth side clients must also be guarded. Abort/timeout never clears unsettled work or authorizes owner/store release.

requirements.title: One optional Task authority
requirements.statement: Where explicit Task integration is used, select one authoritative Task database, retain durable run admission receipts outside it and require current lease/fence/worker for state updates. Unknown admission/cancellation retains slot for exact-boundary reconciliation; results/notifications do not create tasks.
requirements.rationale: A broker/journal is not another Task engine and timeout does not prove no external effect.

requirements.title: Working is coordinator state
requirements.statement: Generic Task working means claimed/coordinator processing and may precede external runtime acceptance/model invocation; do not label it recipient model execution or success.
requirements.rationale: Keeps user-visible execution claims tied to actual runtime evidence.
requirements.scope: Optional GenericTextJobs/A2A/NATS state projection

requirements.title: No loop or privilege fallback
requirements.statement: Existing cron/jobs retain ownership; receiving or notifying does not automatically create another task/reply. Retries, quotas and reply/rate budgets are finite; reaching a limit stops/holds without new IDs, another model, credentials or weakened auth.
requirements.rationale: Controls duplicated work, reply loops and cost growth while preserving independent responsibilities.

requirements.title: GUI and MCP shared authority
requirements.statement: GUI and MCP operations use the same application services, validation, current authorization, idempotency and state meanings. Same verified actor/scope/target/input yields the same business result; no GUI direct-DB bypass.
requirements.rationale: Different entry points must not introduce parallel authority or inconsistent outcomes.

requirements.title: Honest product capability and evidence
requirements.statement: Require verified formal caller/session binding, native transport, durable stores and actual display/input/wake capabilities; unsupported APIs remain unsupported. Synthetic/loopback/injected scheduler proofs must not become actual product model, approval UI, real timing, residency or production E2E claims.
requirements.rationale: Prevents a successful local harness from concealing missing product capabilities.
requirements.scope: Readiness, public capability advertisement and verification reports

requirements.title: Private UI and product simplicity
requirements.statement: Provide human-readable connect/register/select/send and separate connection/registration/receive ability. Private PC/mobile access still requires app authentication/authorization; browser lifetime and public Funnel are not private/resident receive guarantees. Kanban stays separate optional application.
requirements.rationale: The product should hide protocol mechanics while exposing honest capability and operational boundaries.
requirements.scope: Confirmed product goals; manual/live acceptance remains required

requirements.title: Public source versus private runtime
requirements.statement: Keep real credentials, personal messages/history, connection settings and operational raw logs outside the public repo. Source commit/push is not consent for new credentials/grants/public routes/resident processes/fees or real agent execution.
requirements.rationale: Protects personal context and prevents publishing source from expanding operational scope.
requirements.scope: Publication and operational handoff

requirements.title: Restore conservatively
requirements.statement: Quiesce delivery and execution before restoring; reconcile original IDs, epochs, ACK/inbox, known Task/run and external outcomes before resuming. A code rollback that keeps the same delivery journal is allowed only to a build that opens that journal's schema; never rewrite a schema version or rewind the journal or broker store alone. Rolling back past a schema change (the JetStream-only release writes journal schema 4, which earlier builds refuse) restores every part of one consistent pre-upgrade backup generation together and reconciles by original sender and message ID, before routing traffic, each message the newer release accepted and each message still `staging`, `pending`, `leased` or `quarantined` in the backup, because the newer release may have delivered it after the backup; the list takes the union of both journals' IDs and retained recipient evidence, so an ID incomplete in the backup whose row the upgraded journal already purged stays listed with no final state. It also reconciles every body a restored recipient inbox holds unreleased, because an ACK proves only the save: the upgraded recipient may have executed a body acked before the backup, and the restored inbox would hand it to the application again. No journal state proves that a recipient did not save or execute a message: a recipient can save a body while its ACK never commits, leaving the row `expired` or `quarantined`, so those states mean outcome unknown; only `acked` is conclusive, and only of the save, and the recipient's own inbox, Task results and execution records decide the rest. Before the restore, copy the schema 4 journal and every post-upgrade recipient inbox, Task Store, execution record and host `a2a-*.sqlite` file, export from each recipient's copied execution records the sender and message IDs its application handled, and build the list from the copies with the read-only scripts/relay-rollback-reconcile.mjs (`--inbox` per inbox copy, `--backup-inbox` per inbox the restore puts back, `--execution-record` per export). It marks each ID `delivered` (`acked` or a record in its recipient's inbox copy), `not_saved` (`expired` or `quarantined` with no record in an inbox copy that cannot yet have collected it) or `unknown` (no inbox copy, a record that may have been collected, or a purged row with no inbox record); under `restored_bodies` it marks each unreleased backup-inbox body `do_not_process` (listed as handled in its recipient's execution record), `process` (not handled and still unreleased in the upgraded inbox copy) or `unknown` (released in the copy with no execution record, or a copy missing); and it prints `restored_incomplete_expire_by`. Keep the earlier build stopped with no listener until the backup time plus one hour plus the largest `max_clock_skew_ms`, and at least until `restored_incomplete_expire_by`, so every restored ID has expired and the relay does not deliver again anything a recipient saved or executed after the backup. That hold does not cover a body already saved in a restored inbox, which the inbox hands out whatever its expiry, so before restarting each restored recipient settle its `restored_bodies`: record a `do_not_process` body's result in the restored application store under the same sender and message ID and release it with `releaseBody` without handing it to the application, let a `process` body be processed as usual, and keep a recipient with an `unknown` body stopped until its operator decides from its own records, never processing it to find out. Then settle every listed ID: never resend a `delivered` one, tell the sender a `not_saved` one was not delivered (a new attempt is a new request under a new ID), and report an `unknown` one as unknown, without retry, until its recipient's operator checks. Keep the journal and state copies until reconciliation is complete. Do not assume a rollback means unexecuted, dual-dispatch to old/new backends, or promise powerloss/all-copy durability from normal reopen/sync settings. The evidence union also includes IDs absent from the backup that survive only in upgraded inbox or application execution records after journal collection; execution-only evidence has unknown expiry and does not invent a relay save. IDs absent from every supplied source cannot be enumerated and require independent sender/application records. Separately, `retained_bodies` lists unreleased upgraded-copy bodies not restored unreleased: handled ones are `do_not_process`, a body absent from a supplied backup inbox and absent from a supplied execution export is `review_application_handoff`, and missing or conflicting evidence is `unknown`. Draining and waiting do not transfer these bodies. Before recipient restart, review full Task/execution and external-effect state; only a proven unhanded-off body may continue through an application-specific local recovery using a working copy and the original sender/message and Task/run identities with durable deduplication. Never resubmit it to the relay, inject an expired delivery through inbox.save, replace its ID or extend expiry. Preserve evidence; if prior effects are uncertain or no safe recovery exists, keep the recipient stopped. No generic automatic replay or recovery executor is introduced.
requirements.rationale: Restoring old local proof can erase knowledge without undoing remote effects.
requirements.scope: Backup/restore/migration and evidence claims. The reconciliation listing is covered in js-root by test/relay-rollback-reconcile.test.js on a real JetStream journal and agent SDK inboxes, including restored inbox bodies executed or still unprocessed after the backup and an incomplete-at-backup ID whose upgraded row was purged; a third drill on its own broker backs up and restores the journal with the JetStream store dir, the recipient inbox and its application store, runs the listing on the copies, settles the do_not_process body, waits out the hold to restored_incomplete_expire_by, and restarts the relay and the recipient on the restored state, then checks that the broker runs on the backup's stream, the relay delivers nothing again and nothing is executed twice. It restarts the current build on the restored state; starting the earlier build remains production-operations. The extended real-broker drill also leaves a post-backup ACKed body unprocessed, then recovers that saved body locally under its original key after its TTL from a private working copy with the relay stopped. Minimal SQLite projection tests in test/relay-rollback-reconcile-unit.test.js cover journal-GCed new IDs, application-only evidence and missing/conflicting copies; these fixtures do not wait out actual journal retention or prove arbitrary application recovery. The 150,000-incomplete-row SQLite projection regression exercises the CLI entry function, verifies latest expiry without spread-argument overflow, preserves unknown outcomes and checks unchanged journal hashes. The implementation still materializes the read-only listing in memory; this is not an unbounded scalability or production-sizing guarantee.

requirements.title: Optional approval profile proposal
requirements.statement: If an optional asynchronous Task integration adopts the proposed A2A recipient-owner approval profile, keep receiver authenticated approval, operation/content/target hash, epoch/expiry and consumption records separate from sender input; negotiate profile schema/version before implementation.
requirements.rationale: A proposed profile must not be mistaken for existing standard-state functionality or general messaging prerequisite.
requirements.scope: Optional future Task/profile implementation only

requirements.title: Transport adoption is separate
requirements.statement: JetStream delivery is adopted as the only delivery backend (ADR-016), with no dual-send to a second store and no migration of messages held by the retired SQLite store. Evaluate A2A transport adoption using isolated compatible failure/recovery/migration/value tests before formal adoption; do not dual-send the same request or infer closed-product wake/input capabilities from a standard.
requirements.rationale: Existing optional code and a successful lab do not decide production adoption.
requirements.scope: Product0.1 transport adoption and rollout: JetStream delivery is adopted; A2A transport adoption remains future.

requirements.title: Common transport and recipient authority
requirements.statement: Standard HAB transport authenticates and authorizes delivery; the receiving agent retains content judgment, execution and its existing approval rules. No product runner or product-specific approval layer is required by standard connection.
requirements.rationale: Transport consent and sender assertions cannot impersonate recipient-owner approval.
requirements.scope: Standard common MCP Relay; legacy Task integration remains optional.

requirements.title: Approved authentication groups
requirements.statement: One approved authentication group may authenticate one or multiple registered addresses; addresses/inboxes remain distinct and credential sharing within that group is allowed. Product names do not determine authentication or delivery.
requirements.rationale: Provides practical shared host authentication without falsely claiming per-Bot credential isolation.
requirements.scope: Explicit authentication_groups mode; retain legacy1:1 behavior when disabled.

requirements.title: Authorized own-side selection
requirements.statement: Every basic operation validates selected own-side address membership, active state and intersected operation grants. Multiple ambiguous candidates, foreign-group names and expected ID mismatch fail closed. Submit destinations use separate cross-group delivery policy.
requirements.rationale: An address selector is a consistency/routing choice inside authenticated authority, not an authority grant.
requirements.scope: Five HAB Relay operations in group mode.

requirements.title: Stable send and receipt identities
requirements.statement: Persist selected sender/receiver identity and resolved destination with original message intent; recovery reuses original outbox/inbox/ACK identity and never falls back by removing unsupported selectors or re-resolving to another recipient.
requirements.rationale: Prevents duplicate sends and cross-mailbox receipt substitution after restart or address/config change.
requirements.scope: HAB common client and durable sender/receiver integration.

requirements.title: Current authorization through commit
requirements.statement: Recheck current credential, group membership, address/peer state and operation/block policy under registry write guard through Relay commit; bounded scoped authority cannot escape callback or revive stale contexts.
requirements.rationale: Closes revocation-versus-delivery races and prevents stale authorization reuse.
requirements.scope: HAB Registry-composed JetStream delivery (HabJetStreamService); separate IO already sent cannot be retracted.

requirements.title: Separate management authority
requirements.statement: Delivery credentials/tools cannot create groups, enroll names, change membership, add operation grants or perform management rename. Management requires current separate host-verified authority and stable idempotent requests.
requirements.rationale: Receiving a message or selecting a known name must not expand trust or administrative rights.
requirements.scope: HAB registry administration and all optional metadata tools.

requirements.title: Explicit schema and rollback boundary
requirements.statement: Group schema migration is explicit opt-in, preserves existing identities/bindings and refuses old runtimes. Never lower schema version or restore stale online state that resurrects revoked authority or loses accepted deliveries. Keep DB, keys, config and release in a consistent protected backup set.
requirements.rationale: Authority and delivery history must survive migration/recovery; version edits are not safe rollback.
requirements.scope: Registry groupv1→v2 migration and deployment/recovery; proposed renamev3 remains separate.

requirements.title: Participation is separate from token lifetime
requirements.statement: Persistent mode requires explicit OAuthv2 participation dates/state and a short-lived access-token maximum1–900seconds. Legacyv1 remains at most15minutes without auto-upgrade. Refresh cannot extend human participation, widen permissions or change group membership. Context expires no later than token or participation end.
requirements.rationale: Continuous use must not mean unbounded token authority or repeated manual recreation of stable identities.
requirements.scope: Persistent Relay OAuthv2; actual production durations require separate concrete approval.

requirements.title: Host owns OAuth secrets and refresh
requirements.statement: Relay stores approval/binding and validates tokens but does not issue, persist or refresh access/refresh-token bodies. Standard host OAuth client/issuer owns protected secret storage and refresh; failure/expiry/revocation stops use and reports required reauthentication.
requirements.rationale: Keeps credential lifecycle outside model and common message core, and prevents token refresh from granting new trust.
requirements.scope: Relay ingress and common MCP host integration; real issuer/host compatibility remains acceptance work.

requirements.title: Persistent connections survive acceptance
requirements.statement: Keep persistent connection configuration, grant, DB and store keys after a successful roundtrip. Revoke explicitly and narrowly for requested stop/incident, preserving revocation history; RT revocation alone does not prove immediate AT refusal.
requirements.rationale: Acceptance tests should not silently dismantle intended continuing service or erase recovery evidence.
requirements.scope: Persistentv2; finitev1 trial cleanup remains a separate scoped runbook.

requirements.title: Pinned Relay OAuth verification
requirements.statement: Optional Relay OAuth ingress verifies operator-pinned RSA public keys, exact issuer and single canonical resource audience, verified subject/client, required five Relay scopes and bounded token times. Revalidate current configuration before issuing/using opaque contexts. Caller names, headers and unverified JWT claims cannot choose identity or keys.
requirements.rationale: Avoids unsigned authority, confused audiences, attacker-selected key fetching and stale async authentication.
requirements.scope: Pinned Relay OAuth ingress; separate legacy Auth0 resource server has its own bounded JWKS cache contract.

requirements.title: Explicit fail-closed local startup
requirements.statement: Start only with explicit canonical owner-private bounded config/state/keys, required finite capacities and a verifier/audit. Missing/invalid configuration fails before usable operation; empty credential sets deny all. An out-of-range limit, including a `registry` limit, is refused at start as `config_invalid` naming its field, using the same schema the component itself enforces. No fixture fallback, automatic public bind, credential generation or product execution occurs.
requirements.rationale: Prevents accidental anonymous service, secret exposure and unbounded acceptance from example configuration.
requirements.scope: Configured local Relay with its single `delivery` section, and optional ingress.

requirements.title: Owned release and service lifecycle
requirements.statement: Use an explicitly reviewed pinned release/executable/config and stop only owned processes/listeners. Port/state collision fails without commandeering existing services; orderly stop closes resources and preserves accepted state and keys. LaunchAgent supervision does not imply recipient polling or execution.
requirements.rationale: Avoids interfering with unrelated services and overstating infrastructure readiness.
requirements.scope: Local Relay host and optional user LaunchAgent runbook.

requirements.title: Discovery separates name and host identity
requirements.statement: Opt-in read-only discovery distinguishes authenticated group, selected address, trusted host session attestation, registration and unobserved presence. Unknown/stale attestation stays unknown; no inferred offline/available/ownership. Directory remains own-group scoped and occupancy checks neither reserve nor grant.
requirements.rationale: Shared credentials and registration are not proof of which real Bot/session is running.
requirements.scope: Optional hab_discover; basic five-tool behavior remains default.

requirements.title: Limited trial durable ACK evidence
requirements.statement: Before a trial ACK persist complete original envelope and exact generation/lease/ACK request in private per-address durable storage, independently reread and compare, then use that exact request for ACK/reconciliation. Poll/ACK or model conversation memory alone does not prove durable handoff.
requirements.rationale: Separates wire acknowledgements from receiver-owned durable evidence without claiming broad exactly-once or crash guarantees.
requirements.scope: Finite single-consumer trial recipe; coordinator must map stronger common Adapter/supervisor requirements separately.

requirements.title: Redacted evidence and honest identity provenance
requirements.statement: Do not publish secrets, live tenant/client/subject values, personal conversation, DB/config/logs or credentials. Record group and selected identity separately without claiming unique Bot execution; hashes and synthetic fixture roundtrips do not prove live process identity, real OAuth refresh or deployment.
requirements.rationale: Verification evidence must be safe to publish and accurately bounded.
requirements.scope: Public repository and verification output; detailed audit formats remain subsystem-specific.

requirements.title: Original-run reconciliation
requirements.statement: Unknown legacy Task admission keeps original run/scope/receipt and execution gate; retry/reconcile original run under trusted current operator authority instead of creating a replacement run or accepting stop ACK as completion proof.
requirements.rationale: Prevents duplicate external execution and false release after uncertain outcomes.
requirements.scope: Optional fixed-task/worker/Runs subsystem only; not required to exchange normal Relay messages.

requirements.title: Address rename remains explicit proposal
requirements.statement: Proposed same-namespace rename retains immutable agent ID and authority/mailbox identities; old names remain reserved and non-forwarding, with separate rename permission, CAS and migration approval. Do not infer rollout or auto-adopt from implemented prototype.
requirements.rationale: Changing names must not reassign authority or silently resolve deployment policy.
requirements.scope: Optional proposed registryv3 rename only.

requirements.title: Group stop is total and re-grants nothing
requirements.statement: Stopping a group, setting its access to stopped or retired, or revoking its last binding stops every active member address and clears its operations in the same transaction, as revoking an individual binding does. Reactivating or rebinding the group re-grants no address: each member is granted again only by its own explicit access change, so a sibling an operator disconnected stays stopped when another member reconnects. Omitted own-side selection counts only active members.
requirements.rationale: A group stop revokes shared authority. Members that stay active, or that a later reconnect of one address silently revives, would undo an operator's disconnect.
requirements.scope: Registry authentication-group mode and the relay:admin group disconnect and reconnect.

requirements.title: Management connect is atomic and explicit
requirements.statement: A group connect creates the group, binds the connection and adds the first address in one Registry transaction, so a refused step (such as binding capacity) leaves no group behind and a retry converges. That transaction requires every right the three separate operations need (group_create, group_bind and group_member), so a context missing any one of them is refused and creates no group, binding or member. An explicitly empty operation list is refused as `invalid_operations`, never read as the default grant of all operations. The management CLI takes group mode from `registry.authentication_groups` in the config, not from the stored registry schema version.
requirements.rationale: Management requests change authority. A partial or misread request must fail without orphan state and must never grant more than the operator named.
requirements.scope: Operator management CLI (`relay:admin connect`) and the Registry `createBoundGroup` port. The per-operation rights are implementation evidence (src/hab/sqlite-registry.ts in source-review.json), covered in js-root by test/hab-auth-groups.test.js; no document states them separately.

requirements.title: Host A2A identity cannot act as a confused deputy
requirements.statement: A2A is off unless the host config has an `a2a` section; without it there is no listener, mailbox file or host identity. When enabled, startup converges the configured identity address idempotently onto one active agent whose only live binding is the reserved in-process principal `urn:hab:host` with ack/poll/status/submit, and refuses to start with a2a_identity_conflict, a2a_identity_revoked, a2a_identity_stopped or a2a_identity_retired instead of repairing such an identity. The identity has no wire credential: an operator or OAuth principal with the `urn:hab:host` issuer authenticates as nobody, and relay:admin connect refuses the identity address with a2a_identity_reserved. Every A2A request is verified with the caller's own credential, whose audience must be the A2A endpoint. The caller must currently hold resolve and submit and be allowed to send execution_request to the configured recipient; that check repeats inside the Registry guard that commits the outbox record and around each send. The host identity's submit runs inside a Registry transaction that first repeats the caller check, because a withRelay called inside another's callback joins its transaction, so a revocation from another connection commits either before that check, which refuses the send, or after the message is admitted, never between them. The caller cannot choose sender, recipient, kind or body. Tasks are scoped to the caller's agent ID and the recipient tenant, so another caller cannot read them, and a revoked grant or disconnection makes them unreachable. The fixed host principal remains reserved to its original agent after revocation. Disconnect is a permanent A2A off switch for this Registry; changing the identity address cannot undo it. Removing the a2a section permits MCP-only startup without deleting stored history. No identity rotation or revocation reset is provided.
requirements.rationale: The host identity submits under its own rights. Without a current per-request check of the caller it could deliver to a recipient the caller cannot reach, or expose another caller's replies.
requirements.scope: Opt-in host A2A entry (src/host/a2a.ts) with the local bearer verifier only; the OAuth ingress does not serve A2A, and a group-authenticated caller with several addresses is refused. Covered in js-root by test/a2a-host.test.js.

requirements.title: Shared model-free communication core
requirements.statement: Relay wire/core and explicit receive/send cycles transport opaque ordered content without product SDK, model, shell or Task execution; recipient-local integration decides processing separately. Ordinary MCP delivery tools do not expose maintenance, release or execution.
requirements.rationale: A shared language-neutral message path must not inherit any product-specific execution/approval semantics.
requirements.scope: Relay/HAB common delivery and recipient orchestration

requirements.title: Durable recipient save before ACK
requirements.statement: The recipient commits the exact body, dedup identity and stable ACK request before issuing ACK. A failed save sends no ACK; repeated delivery and lost ACK response recover original body/receipt without duplicating inbox entries or claiming execution.
requirements.rationale: ACK authorizes server body disposal, so a committed local receive record must exist first.
requirements.scope: DurableReceiver and recipient-owned SQLite inbox/ACK journal

requirements.title: Immutable versioned message identity and lifetime
requirements.statement: Preserve opaque IDs, JSON keys/strings and body part order under strict version/schema limits; sender is derived from verified policy, timestamps are canonical UTC and original lifetime is exactly one hour. Replays cannot change payload, destination, identity or extend deadline.
requirements.rationale: Cross-language transport and replay must have one consistent semantic message identity.
requirements.scope: Version1 common Relay envelope

requirements.title: Current authority and one fenced recipient lease
requirements.statement: Use current verified operation and sender/kind policy, at most one live recipient lease, bounded scan and original expiry. Initial ACK requires current generation/token/lease; exact committed retry recovers the same delivery receipt without granting execution, using current authority.
requirements.rationale: Stale credentials/leases and caller-selected identities must not cross an immutable individual boundary.
requirements.scope: Server poll/ACK in the JetStream journal, HAB's only delivery backend. The spec's lease and ACK order states the rules; DESIGN.md places them in the journal transaction.

requirements.title: Bounded recovery keeps unknown outcomes
requirements.statement: Persist original immutable intent before network. Recovery uses exact original IDs/body/expiry/ACK requests and finite persisted backoff/attempt/status horizons. Timeout, invalid/missing response, audit failure after commit or status not_found alone do not prove non-delivery; exhaustion may become quarantined/expired_unknown, never replacement message or automatic identity switch.
requirements.rationale: An uncertain side effect cannot be rolled back by pretending a failed response means no commit.
requirements.scope: Sender/outbox and all HTTP/async boundaries

requirements.title: Delivery, reading, application handoff and execution remain separate
requirements.statement: Inbox is a received-message record, not execution queue. Local handoff requires separately durable application save deduplicated by sender/message before explicit release; ACK confirmation and release are independent. No read/release/receipt alone proves exactly-once application effects or Task acceptance. Unreleased body is retained under finite backpressure. The record and byte quotas count unreleased bodies only, so a release frees a slot at once, while a separate finite `max_ack_records` bound limits the dedup history, counted by message, that every saved message enters; a released tombstone still deduplicates. A lease redelivery of a message already in that history adds an ACK row for its new generation without taking another slot, and one message keeps at most `max_attempts` generations (a further one is refused with `inbox_capacity_exceeded`), so the ACK table holds at most `max_ack_records × max_attempts` rows. `releaseUnconfirmable` releases, without handing it to the application, only a body whose receipt can no longer be confirmed: its ACK is unconfirmed, the message has expired so no new generation can be saved, and no ACK request is pending; otherwise it changes nothing, and the released tombstone still deduplicates. Rows of any kind are capped at `max_records + max_ack_records`. A legacy (non-replay-bound) ID's tombstone is never collected, because a replay of it could not be told from a new message, so legacy-ID rows are capped at `max_ack_records`: a new legacy ID past that is refused with `inbox_legacy_id_capacity_exceeded`, replay-bound IDs keep the `max_records` body budget, and a held legacy ID stays deduplicated and is never handed off again. hasCapacityFor(records, bodyBytes) is a read-only check for new replay-bound messages against body/byte, per-message ACK-history and retained-row bounds; it neither reserves nor collects and never shortens retention from actual local terminal time. An optional original-source (sender_id, message_id) hint limits SQLite inbox reads through an additive partial expression index over unreleased bodies. It includes pending ACKs, preserves ordering, excludes released empty bodies, and changes neither record format/version nor retention. The hint never replaces receipt, identity, reference, thread, schema or current-authorization checks; unfiltered route implementations remain compatible.
requirements.rationale: Receiver storage and user processing have different lifetimes and authority boundaries.
requirements.scope: Recipient-local body lifecycle. The quota and row bounds, the per-message ACK history, the `max_attempts` generation cap `releaseUnconfirmable` and the collection of replay-bound IDs over repeated retention cycles are covered in js-root by test/relay-inbox-maintenance.test.js. The same suite covers the read-only capacity gate and unchanged terminal-time retention.

requirements.title: Bounded metadata collection preserves replay safety
requirements.statement: Explicit finite maintenance erases expired server body and only collects terminal metadata after required original expiry/terminal/ACK or status retry horizons plus retention. Reads/exact retry do not renew dates. Time-bound rm1 IDs bind original timestamp; legacy or malformed opaque identities remain safety-held instead of opening a replay window. Safety-held records never take a maintenance batch slot, so a held backlog cannot starve collection of due replay-bound records. Logical deletion does not imply physical erase or backup removal.
requirements.rationale: Finite storage cannot erase dedup evidence while stale requests remain admissible.
requirements.scope: JetStream journal (server, DESIGN.md), and the agent SDK's sender outbox and receiver inbox tombstone maintenance. Replay-bound retention cycles are covered for the inbox in js-root by "replay-bound IDs are collected every retention cycle, so new IDs keep saving within the row bound and a collected ID is never handed off again" (five cycles under a one-slot cap: nothing collected before retention ends, every row collected after it, a replay of a collected ID refused as expired_delivery), and for the journal by the P7 nats-producer case "replay-bound IDs cycle through the record cap every retention period, and a collected ID is never delivered again" (three cycles under a two-record cap with a mocked clock: capacity_exceeded until collection, a replay inside retention answered with the acked receipt and not delivered, a collected ID refused as expired_before_acceptance and not delivered).

requirements.title: Attachments are explicit bounded optional composition
requirements.statement: Retired (historical): managed attachments were removed. The contract has no attachment part and the upload, binding, read and attachment MCP/HTTP modules were deleted. HAB-D18 replaces this requirement with refusal of attachment parts. Original accepted statement, kept for provenance: Defaults continue rejecting attachment storage/delivery until required host ports are explicitly connected. Original verified owner, immutable intent and manifest bind one-hour message identity; finalize, acceptance, receipt, execution are separate. Strict finite chunks/codecs prohibit arbitrary URL/path/free tool or body execution.
requirements.rationale: The removed design cannot be verified against code that no longer exists. Keeping the ID with its original text preserves provenance without enforcing it.
requirements.scope: Removed attachment upload/read/admission/delivery/client; no current scope.

requirements.title: Verified local attachment bytes gate body save and ACK
requirements.statement: Retired (historical): the attachment inbox, receive checkpoint and AttachmentReceiver were deleted. DurableReceiver save-before-ACK (HAB-D02) is the only receive path. Original accepted statement, kept for provenance: Durably stage original-message chunks with original offset and integrity, verify all declared files/lengths/order/SHA including empty files, and recheck retained bytes under synchronous guard before body/ACK save and ACK claim. Missing, corrupt, unverified or prematurely released bytes cause no ACK. Checkpoint cannot issue ACK and does not replace body inbox.
requirements.rationale: Attachment bytes no longer exist on any path, so the gate has nothing to protect.
requirements.scope: Removed AttachmentInbox and AttachmentReceiver; no current scope.

requirements.title: Cross-DB commits reconcile original records
requirements.statement: Retired (historical): the upload acceptance, attachment outbox handoff, receive checkpoint and attachment deletion stores were deleted, so these cross-DB commit pairs no longer exist. HAB-D05 still covers original-ID recovery for messages. Original accepted statement, kept for provenance: Treat prepare→Relay commit→confirm, source→outbox handoff, body save→checkpoint clear and deletion→job done as independent commits, not distributed rollback. Preserve original reservations/intent/body/checkpoint where needed and reconcile original ID/job/receipt/fence after response or local commit uncertainty. No new IDs or deadline extension.
requirements.rationale: The independent stores this requirement coordinated were removed.
requirements.scope: Removed attachment upload acceptance, outbox handoff, checkpoint and server deletion; no current scope.

requirements.title: Terminal disposal and local release are distinct
requirements.statement: Retired (historical): attachment terminal deletion jobs and retained recipient bytes were removed. Relay schema 6 drops the deletion tables and inbox schema 4 drops the attachment columns. Original accepted statement, kept for provenance: ACK/expiry atomically stores exact minimal protected deletion job with server terminal state/body erasure/audit; unfinished jobs prevent ownership GC. A finite maintenance-authorized fenced worker deletes only exact terminal binding bytes and reconciles unknown completion. Server access closes at ACK; local verified bytes remain until explicit durable application handoff and ACK reconciliation permit release.
requirements.rationale: No attachment bytes are stored, so there is no deletion job or retained blob to track.
requirements.scope: Removed server attachment deletion and recipient retained bytes; no current scope.

requirements.title: Admission capacity is finite and atomic
requirements.statement: Host-selected positive finite count/byte/record caps and minimum reservations are evaluated using verified immutable identity and persisted usage in the same admission transaction. Exact replay/conflict precedes new quota; retained metadata still counts, and capacity shrink does not discard accepted work.
requirements.rationale: Backpressure protects other individuals and bounded storage without corrupting recovery evidence.
requirements.scope: Required delivery.queue.agent_capacity policy in the JetStream journal. The attachment owner_capacity policy was removed with attachments.

requirements.title: Scope fair selection separately from rate and execution
requirements.statement: Fair polling durably advances bounded sender/message cursors with lease/audit while denied candidates consume no delivery attempt; keep one live recipient lease and rollback corruption. Shared one-process writer uses finite identity map/queues, monotonic token bucket, fresh identity before callback and no DB locks while waiting. Retain active slot until actual callback/audit settles after timeout. Neither mechanism guarantees byte/time/model fairness, fleet rate or SLO.
requirements.rationale: Choice-count fairness and finite process admission must not be advertised as end-to-end execution scheduling guarantees.
requirements.scope: Opt-in delivery.queue.fair_poll in the JetStream journal and WriterAdmission

requirements.title: Snapshot restore requires offline original-ID reconciliation
requirements.statement: Retired (historical): SQLiteSnapshotBundle was deleted with the attachment modules and its document was removed. Whole-state JetStream backup and restore stays an operations gate (OPERATIONS.md) under HAB-F24 and the open HAB-C-D04. Original accepted statement, kept for provenance: Capture every DB in one fixed profile under all writer locks, validate private canonical owner/schema/bytes, preserve signed fixed-file manifests and never overwrite existing state. Exclude authority/config/secrets/Task and do not roll back current stop/revocation. Restore only new offline directory; marker is not an enforcement boundary. Host must quiesce IO and reconcile original receipts/IDs/leases/current authority and unknown remote effects before promotion.
requirements.rationale: The snapshot profiles named the retired SQLite Relay store and attachment DBs, none of which exist now.
requirements.scope: Removed SQLiteSnapshotBundle profiles; no current scope.

requirements.title: JetStream admission, journal rules and recipient receipt remain distinct
requirements.statement: Keep synchronous fresh Registry guard around durable admission/poll/ACK; supervised broker I/O cannot carry scoped authorization over await or create recipient lease during prefetch. JetStream is the only delivery backend: each former store rule (reciprocal pair-scoped replies, global/recipient/per-sender capacity and reservations, exact retry without new capacity, one application lease, fair poll) commits in the journal transaction that changes state. Broker unavailability keeps admitted bodies in the bounded outbox under the same IDs, with no SQLite fallback. Recipient saves first; saved HAB ACK then tracks later broker erasure, never Task completion.
requirements.rationale: Replacing the storage backend must preserve the common message and receiver-owned execution contract.
requirements.scope: HAB JetStream delivery, the only delivery backend. The SQLite store, router and routing epochs were retired.

requirements.title: Pinned private broker and bounded durability claims
requirements.statement: Use fixed finite File/one-replica/Limits/DiscardNew broker configuration and verified pinned runtime, current original HAB deadline and exact subject/content reconciliation. Persistent volume marker/device checks fail closed without fallback state; inspect actual fsync policy instead of inferring it from client INFO. requirements.title: Attachment parts are refused on every delivery path

A submission that carries an attachment part, in any position, or a policy that carries a former attachment limit key fails validation before storage on the contract, MCP submit and JetStream paths. No attachment store, upload or download tool exists.
