requirements.scope: Version-1 messaging contract, MCP submit and JetStream delivery

requirements.title: Journal delivery audit is atomic and redacted
requirements.statement: The JetStream journal records accepted, leased, requeued, quarantined, expired and acked events with sender, message ID and time only, never body or token, in the same transaction as the state change. An audit failure rolls back that admission, lease or ACK including its capacity use. Missing maintenance totals fail closed instead of losing counts.
requirements.rationale: The retired SQLite store committed audit with state; moving delivery to the journal must keep evidence that cannot diverge from delivery state or leak content.
requirements.scope: JetStream journal schema 4 delivery audit and maintenance totals

requirements.title: Host A2A sends only inside the owner's request
requirements.statement: The host A2A outbox, inbox and SDK Task store are private 0600 files in the host state directory; a saved Task, its send intent and received replies survive a host restart, and a replay reuses the original message ID and one-hour expiry. A saved intent is sent only inside its owner's authorized SendMessage, which claims only that message ID from the shared outbox. There is no background submit retry; a retry is a repeated SendMessage with the same messageId. The only background work is the receiver loop, which polls the host mailbox and classifies each delivery before saving anything. A new reply ID is classified against the stored Task and only ACK-confirmed held replies. If it cannot change that state or is refused by validated contract/schema rules, it is discarded with ACK and no inbox record. If it would change that state but would be redundant or conflicting assuming an unconfirmed held reply became usable, it is deferred without save or ACK. Unexpected preview failures also defer rather than proving redundancy. A deferred delivery remains subject to finite relay leases, attempts and TTL, so it may quarantine or expire; recovery is not guaranteed. An ID already held still reaches the inbox for deduplication and ACK confirmation. Unconfirmed replies are never applied. Any other delivery is ACKed without an inbox record or ACK history entry, so unrelated senders spend none of the capacity replies need; dropping it again on a redelivery is harmless, so it needs no dedup record. At most once a minute the loop runs bounded inbox and outbox maintenance. Window closure uses at most 100 overdue Tasks per receive cycle, ordered and paged by the complete stable (tenant, owner, id) key. The cursor advances past individual failed applies; a full page schedules another cycle, and the end resets the cursor for the next scheduled pass. The earliest open window or at most one minute schedules that pass. Thus a failed full batch does not permanently hide later Tasks, but a backlog or persistent storage failure does not promise every transition within one cycle. `max_records` caps the outbox. The inbox holds `2 × max_records` unreleased reply bodies, one `execution_accepted` and one `execution_result` per host message, so an accepted reply never takes the slot its own result needs. The receiver loop applies each ACKed reply to its Task and releases the body once the Task store holds the new state; a reply the Task refuses (a conflict, a malformed body, such as a late reply to a terminal Task, or one over the A2A contract limits) is released the same way, and any other failure keeps the body for the next cycle. A successful durable apply releases the body even without a caller read; unexpected storage failures retain it for retry. A saved reply whose ACK never committed is never applied; once it has expired with no ACK request pending, so no redelivery can confirm it, the loop releases its body unread with `releaseUnconfirmable` and keeps its tombstone for dedup, and its Task waits for another reply or for its reply window to close. A reply is saved only while the current time is before its request's expiry plus one day (the reply window); a later reply is ACKed without a record and does not change its Task. Each outbox record is kept for at least the reply window plus the one-day ACK retry plus two hours past its expiry, then 30 days. That horizon alone cannot outlive an ACK first made terminal after a long stop: the required 30 days from its actual local terminal time are preserved. Maintenance collects the inbox first, then computes a bounded outbox collection allowance. Let M be max_records, T be retained outbox rows, W be retained sources whose reply windows are still open (expires_at > now minus one day), and p be proposed collected rows. It binary-searches p from 0 through 100 against room for 2 × (max(0, M - T + p) + W) new replies. For T <= M this equals 2 × (F + W + p), where F = M - T. If an operator lowers M below T, collecting excess rows creates no usable sender slots until the count falls below M. The check includes those replies and their maximum envelope bytes, checking unreleased body/byte, distinct-message ACK-history and all retained-row capacities. This preserves two future replies for each free slot and open source before freeing additional sender slots. The snapshots and numeric-cap collection have no intervening await in the single-owner host. Only eligible rows are collected, and expiry still runs even when the allowance is zero. This is conservative capacity accounting, not a multi-writer reservation or shortened retention. The inbox keeps an ACK history of three times `max_records` messages for the same 30 days, counted per message, so the lease redeliveries of one reply (up to `max_attempts` generations) take a single slot. A blocking SendMessage holds the handler's Task serializer only for each 25 ms check, which reloads the stored Task, so the receiver loop applies replies during the five-second wait and a result saved in a later receive cycle than its acceptance completes the Task. On close the host refuses new A2A requests with 503 and waits for in-flight requests and the current receiver cycle before closing its stores, leaving unsent intents, unACKed deliveries and saved Tasks on disk. Closing the Task store must close its eagerly opened SQLite connection even if the lazy SDK database driver was never initialized by a load/save, and repeated close is safe. An optional original-source (sender_id, message_id) hint limits SQLite inbox reads through an additive partial expression index over unreleased bodies. It includes pending ACKs, preserves ordering, excludes released empty bodies, and changes neither record format/version nor retention. The hint never replaces receipt, identity, reference, thread, schema or current-authorization checks; unfiltered route implementations remain compatible.
requirements.rationale: A background resend under the host identity would send without a current check of the caller who asked for it; save-before-ACK keeps replies recoverable across a crash.
requirements.scope: Opt-in host A2A entry, one host process per state directory. Not multi-host writer coordination, production retention or capacity design. Covered in js-root by test/a2a-host.test.js, including results saved when accepted replies fill the cap, unread completed Tasks freeing their slots after the outbox purge, a Task admitted after a purge whose replies are saved after a late reply, unconfirmable saved replies that release their slots so a later reply still completes its Task, and a blocking SendMessage completing from a result in a later receive cycle than its acceptance. Its case "a saved confirmed reply that breaks the A2A contract limits is released as refused and leaves its Task unchanged" saves and ACK-confirms, offline, an execution_result whose data part is over HAB_A2A_LIMITS, then checks that the running host releases the body instead of retrying it every cycle and that the Task stays SUBMITTED. Its case "a flood of fresh-ID replies that would not change the Task takes no ACK history, so the valid result still completes it" sends more repeated acceptances, conflicting acceptances and refused results under fresh IDs than the `3 × max_records` ACK history holds, then a valid result, and checks that the result completes the Task with only two inbox rows. "when the running host loses its own ACK of a saved result, the reply expires unapplied and a new result still completes the Task" drops the running host's ACKs of one result at its delivery-service transport while the result is live, then checks the real relay's invalid_ack, the unapplied release and completion from a new result. "a Task whose reply window closes while the host runs fails within seconds, not at the next once-a-minute maintenance" covers the window timing (HAB-E20). The long-stop regression uses a 500 ms lease and injected host ACK transport failures to leave acceptance and result ACKs pending before one stop. It models 40 days offline by shifting timestamps and replay-bound IDs, verifies new Task refusal while local-terminal history is retained, then models another 31 days and verifies admission and both replies recover through normal maintenance. It is not a real 71-day outage or an unconditional downtime claim. This gate prevents future outbox collection; it does not restore source slots an earlier build already purged, repair already lost/quarantined results, or establish spare capacity in an existing deployment. Before resuming an affected deployment, quiesce new A2A admissions and let normal inbox maintenance and the full 30-day retention from actual local terminal time restore sufficient capacity. Do not delete history, shorten retention or re-execute Tasks with unknown outcomes. The bounded allowance remains conservative and does not repair previously lost admission reservations. No live deployment has been checked. test/a2a-sdk-store.test.js covers unused eager connection closure after direct host maintenance reads, closure after SDK initialization, safe repeated close and reopening. This demonstrates the lifecycle defect and its repair, not a universal cause or repair for malformed databases. The outage fixture now ages first_sent_at consistently with the replay-bound ID and expires_at, uses the host Task-store driver for offline Task metadata changes and checks integrity before reopening. It checks the old Task reaches FAILED after its result window and retries only outbox_capacity_exceeded, surfacing other errors immediately without increasing the timeout. A held confirmed body is retained on an unexpected per-Task save failure; no exception-based blanket release is allowed. The mixed-cohort regression injects that failure for one legitimate Task, verifies partial collection and another Task completing while the body remains, then removes the fault and verifies recovery. It does not repair malformed SQLite pages, a globally failed database or invalid JSON that prevents inbox enumeration. Cohort aging changes rm1 IDs and timestamps consistently but does not refresh fingerprints, so it is maintenance/capacity evidence, not a whole-state restore proof. The shutdown controls demonstrate a saved Task retrying under its original identity after close, and synchronous claim-to-admission before a queued close; no normal-shutdown race fix is claimed. The overdue control injects 100 per-Task save failures before a healthy later Task, then removes the fault and checks wrap/retry. It does not establish corrupt metadata reachability through the API.

requirements.title: Optional execution must not become messaging prerequisite
requirements.statement: Ordinary common-MCP messaging and receive-only supervisor work without Task, fixed Runs or a Hermes-specific model/approval adapter; receiving agents retain content, execution and existing approval decisions.
requirements.rationale: Communication authority and delivery must not take over recipient execution policy.
requirements.scope: Standard messaging; optional subsystem entrypoints remain explicitly composed.

requirements.title: Storage receipt is not Task or completion
requirements.statement: Receiving and ACK do not create a Task; separate current local accept and independently authenticated Task submit are required. Completion/result emission requires saved matching terminal evidence with execution_open=0.
requirements.rationale: Avoid interpreting transportation success as authorization or execution success.
requirements.scope: Explicit fixed TaskBridge and the A2A Relay preview composed with HabExecutionEvidence only; the host-routed A2A entry is reply-attested under HAB-E20 and never satisfies this completion rule; ordinary message receive stays Task-free.

requirements.title: Unknown execution cannot trigger fresh work
requirements.statement: Save stable key and original scope/deadline before external admission. Unknown execution may only reconcile original key/known run; timeout, abort, missing lookup result or expired retention never establish no external effect and never authorize a fresh key/create.
requirements.rationale: An ambiguous external call could already have committed; fresh work could duplicate effects.
requirements.scope: Explicit execution integrations; fixed TaskBridge may resubmit only through its same-key engine idempotency contract.

requirements.title: Coordinator and unknown state stay truthful
requirements.statement: working means coordinator claim, including before remote runtime acceptance; lease uncertainty is execution_reconciliation, unconfirmed cancellation is cancellation_confirmation with unknown outcome. Neither means owner approval, model running, successful termination or permission to retry.
requirements.rationale: Status projection must not imply unobserved execution or transfer owner authority.
requirements.scope: Optional generic Task A2A/MCP/NATS projection.

requirements.title: Message fields cannot select execution authority
requirements.statement: Resolve verified subject/client, full binding and current operation-specific authority at each action; message text, names, ROLE_USER and claimed approval do not create principals, owner scope, recipient or permissions. Distinct clients remain distinct even for same human.
requirements.rationale: Authenticated transport body is not a recipient-owner grant.
requirements.scope: Optional generic jobs, bridge and receiver-host handoff; no production identity is established by synthetic fixtures.

requirements.title: Reply loops and budget are finite
requirements.statement: Automated host replies only allow question→answer and execution_request→accepted/result with one stable reply per source/kind; replies/notices/failures cannot recursively generate answers or Tasks. Explicit finite shared budget is committed before outbox and never refunded to recover unknown delivery.
requirements.rationale: Bounds prevent self-amplifying communication, quota bypass and duplicate reply effects.
requirements.scope: Recipient-local automated reply host and optional TaskReplies when budget explicitly connected; proposed8/thread60/min are not defaults.

requirements.title: Durable answer before handoff
requirements.statement: Persist one decided answer envelope before budget/outbox handoff; same source replay reuses original ID/body/deadline. Uncertain cross-DB result remains prepared and is reconciled with same envelope. Startup/listing/expiry does not send, invent new answer, Task or deadline.
requirements.rationale: Prepared replies survive restart without recreating content from conversation or duplicating unknown handoff.
requirements.scope: Optional AnswerIntents producer and its host wiring.

requirements.title: Stop epoch is atomic but not remote cancellation
requirements.statement: Bind verified principal to current durable epoch and validate gate with local Task effects atomically. Restore invalidates old requests and never grants identity, restores subscription or retries unknown run. Stop cannot recall sent bytes or prove external model cessation.
requirements.rationale: Prevent stale authority after stop/restore without overstating cross-system atomicity.
requirements.scope: Task authorization and separately authorized notifications; standard receive control covered by other reader.

requirements.title: Owner lock cannot time out into duplicate work
requirements.statement: All hosts for one local identity share dedicated exclusive owner DB; no heartbeat/TTL takeover. Owner loss rejects late save/ACK and release requires paused, not-running and zero draining. Reacquisition alone does not reset execution gate or justify new ID/Task.
requirements.rationale: A slow or timed-out call may still settle after another host begins.
requirements.scope: Optional SQLiteHostOwner; local-MVP composition requires it, legacy unconfigured compatibility is not evidence of owner enforcement. Managed transport is a trusted cooperative local-admission capability: unlike guarded fetch, its check releases the control transaction before physical SDK/IPC send. A request admitted before pause may still commit; every later request/retry needs a new current check. Product OAuth side clients must also be guarded. Abort/timeout never clears unsettled work or authorizes owner/store release.

requirements.title: Generic text protocol preserves bounded exact input
requirements.statement: Optional generic profile accepts only explicit nonblocking structured text with bounded valid Unicode excluding NUL/lone surrogates; max text/result32768UTF8 bytes, request256KiB,response512KiB. No silent replace/truncate/normalization; changed bound payload/deadline on stable ID conflicts.
requirements.rationale: Prevent storage conversion and retry ambiguity while keeping finite protocol resources.
requirements.scope: async-text-v1 and GenericTextJobs; fixed connectivity/ping contracts remain separate.

requirements.title: Capacity does not evict active dedup evidence
requirements.statement: Private execution/reply journals reject binding/key/schema/corruption/capacity failures and preserve existing unknown/dedup records. Reopen does not extend original deadline or convert delivery expiry into failed/nonexistent execution. Independent restore needs quiescent reconciliation.
requirements.rationale: Freeing space or refreshing time cannot erase the only evidence preventing duplicate work.
requirements.scope: TaskBridge and reply journals; exact numeric policies stay subsystem-specific. The optional generic NATS client/recipient was deleted, so its journals are no longer in scope.

requirements.title: Optional inventory import policy agrees in TS and Python
requirements.statement: Inventory-only launcher uses measured fixed noneditable dependencies and pinned -I -S bootstrap before third-party imports; no site/.pth/editable roots or reintroduced excluded packages. TS inspector/Python validator agree; inconclusive EPERM stays fail-closed.
requirements.rationale: Pre-wrapper executable imports could escape fixed tool bounds; mode bits or mock assertions are insufficient.
requirements.scope: Existing optional one-shot inventory executor only; not a universal messaging or normal agent-tools restriction.

requirements.title: Ephemeral key revocation needs confirmed owned stop
requirements.statement: Optional one-shot key stays private runtime-only, persists fingerprint/lifecycle metadata and never token. Confirm child and adapter stop before revoked; otherwise stop_failed with retained receipt/artifact. Parent/helper normal exit is not task success or proof all remote work stopped.
requirements.rationale: Bearer has no intrinsic TTL and strings cannot be reliably zeroized; only owned boundary shutdown can support local revocation.
requirements.scope: Optional LocalHermesKey/inventory factory/manual handoff; not standard-MCP credential requirement.

requirements.title: Live trial cost and quota require evidence
requirements.statement: For optional live diagnostics/inventory with agreed zero-additional-cost ceiling, unknown included allowance/provider billing or quota stops work. No paid fallback, silent credit use, tick token minting or auto retry. Account-wide token attempts reserve durable shared counters and unknown attempts park until reviewed reconciliation.
requirements.rationale: Model-route success and cached plan claims do not establish entitlement, allowance or safe quota.
requirements.scope: User-selected zero-cost optional live trials and token broker; not assertion of current provider prices/plans and no live trial authorized by this contract.

requirements.title: Metadata cannot promote into execution
requirements.statement: Discovery-only/metadata modes create no Task/worker/model authority, reject all task calls and cannot become active by config mutation. Actual authenticated correlated result and owned cleanup are separate acceptance gates.
requirements.rationale: HTTP metadata/readback/200 can otherwise be mistaken for authenticated executable product integration.
requirements.scope: Explicit ping-discovery and inventory-metadata diagnostics; live OAuth/native client readiness remains manual.

requirements.title: Audit acknowledgement is finite and truthful
requirements.statement: Before-action audit must receive bounded writer acknowledgement or deny, with no automatic writer restart. After-action failure cannot undo committed effects and unknown work keeps its admission. Fixed redacted bounded diagnostics do not leak body/token/raw authority; OS write ACK is not fsync.
requirements.rationale: Avoid audit floods blocking event loop or timeout enabling duplicate work; do not overclaim durability.
requirements.scope: Existing Node task runtime/native and portable protocol review fixes, not generic app logging convention.

requirements.title: Proof labels preserve actual exercised scope
requirements.statement: Synthetic model-free loopback/SQLite tests and close/reopen prove their exercised contracts only, never native agent model/approval/wake, kill9/power failure, hosted identity or full operational restore. Finite native fixed-text exchange is separate evidence with pinned revisions and no generic-crash claim.
requirements.rationale: Prevent fixture success being promoted into untested native or operational guarantees.
requirements.scope: All verification claims involving optional execution and local MVP.

requirements.title: Fixed metadata cannot prove product identity
requirements.statement: Fixed lstat inventory reports candidate metadata as unknown and never claims exact installed product or whole-machine absence; no listing, shell, network or broad filesystem fallback.
requirements.rationale: Names/missing fixed paths are insufficient identity/exhaustiveness evidence.
requirements.scope: Optional shift_log_inventory collector only; not standard messaging.

requirements.title: Fixed pilot success remains historical
requirements.statement: Earlier exact fixed-connectivity Hermes Runs success establishes only its finite reviewed route and cannot accept current inventory imports/key lifecycle or ordinary standard-MCP product connection.
requirements.rationale: Earlier route success is useful evidence but not universal architecture or permission.
requirements.scope: Earlier hermes-hub-fixed-pilot-v1 local prototype.

requirements.title: Host-routed A2A completion is reply-attested and labelled
requirements.statement: The host-routed A2A entry has no engine evidence port. Recipient storage ACK leaves the Task SUBMITTED. A durable execution_accepted reply makes it WORKING, and a durable execution_result reply makes it COMPLETED (succeeded, with the result text as the only Artifact), FAILED or CANCELED; an expired or quarantined request with no reply becomes INPUT_REQUIRED until its reply window closes. A reply counts only when the configured recipient sent it, it references that Task's own host source message, its thread matches and its schema is exact. A reply counts only if it arrives before its request's expiry plus one day (the reply window); a later one is ACKed without a record and never changes the Task. By the owner's 2026-11-07 decision (ADR-016), a Task with no result applied when its reply window closes, whether SUBMITTED, WORKING or INPUT_REQUIRED, moves to the standard TASK_STATE_FAILED with no Artifact, `reason: "result_window_expired"` in its status message metadata and its public `hab_relay` metadata, and a status message that starts with `result_window_expired` and says the outcome is unknown, because the recipient may or may not have executed the request; no custom A2A state is added and the Task never stays WORKING. The host receiver loop makes this transition without a caller read through bounded stable-key pages from the Task store's `overdue()`, starting when the earliest window closes; later pages and failed applies can require later cycles. A read after the window attempts the transition at once. A reply arriving afterwards never revives or changes the Task. FAILED with result_window_expired never claims that the recipient did not execute the request. A later reply with another engine Task ID, or a second terminal result with another state, is refused without replacing the saved Task. Every such Task's public metadata carries `attestation: "recipient_reply"`, and the Card and Artifact describe the result as the recipient's report. COMPLETED here claims no verification of the recipient's engine and never satisfies the evidence-verified rule of HAB-E02 and HAB-V12.
requirements.rationale: The host cannot read a remote recipient's engine. The label keeps a recipient's self-report from passing as independently verified execution.
requirements.scope: Opt-in host A2A entry only. The preview composition with HabExecutionEvidence keeps HAB-E02 and HAB-V12. Covered in js-root by test/a2a-host.test.js; an actual product recipient's reply is not exercised. Its case "a WORKING Task whose reply window closes without a result fails as result_window_expired, and a late result does not revive it" ages the request two days while the host is stopped, waits for the stored Task to fail without a caller read, checks the reason, the outcome-unknown message and the empty Artifacts, and checks that a late result is ACKed without a record and leaves the status unchanged. Its case "a Task whose reply window closes while the host runs fails within seconds, not at the next once-a-minute maintenance" ages the request so that its window closes five seconds after a restart, after the restart's first maintenance pass, and checks that the stored Task fails within 20 seconds of that time without a read. A live drive cannot wait out the day (features/a2a-host.md a2a-window). A new unit control holds a pre-window result unconfirmed, reaches FAILED at the window, then confirms it and checks that it cannot revive the failed Task. It preserves the existing deadline semantics, not a new grace period. One-cycle timing is an unobstructed fixture claim, not a backlog guarantee.

requirements.title: Observe action and resulting state
requirements.statement: A mapped feature claim must retain the actual protocol/terminal action, its result and an independent state or peer observation, labeled by sub-feature ID.
requirements.rationale: HTTP 200, a helper exit or a mutated screen alone does not prove the intended side effect.
requirements.scope: HAB local verify-hab recipes; terminal requires transcript plus exit.

requirements.title: Durable receiver evidence precedes network ACK
requirements.statement: To claim durable receipt, independently observe committed recipient body and original ACK request before the actual network ACK; raw poll/ACK and Relay snapshots prove only wire behavior.
requirements.rationale: Relay ACK can delete its body; loss between ACK and durable recipient storage would otherwise be hidden.
requirements.scope: DurableReceiver/SQLiteInbox through real MCP HTTP; independent connection, not native product execution.

requirements.title: Receive preserves content without execution
requirements.statement: The periodic receiver must preserve question/notice/structured request content, leave Task links/Tasks/reply outbox empty, and keep decisions, execution and existing approval with the receiving agent.
requirements.rationale: External content and claimed approval must not become execution authority merely through delivery.
requirements.scope: Standard common-MCP receive path, optional Task port may be configured but is not automatically invoked.

requirements.title: Explicit saved-body read creates no authority
requirements.statement: Saved-body reading must be explicit and source-authorized, preserve ACK-pending truth and return detached data without creating a Task or reply or granting permission to act.
requirements.rationale: An agent needs received data while inspection remains separate from execution and approval.
requirements.scope: Adapter inbox_read operation; native host/UI integration remains separately unverified.

requirements.title: Coordinator working is not model evidence
requirements.statement: Do not treat optional Task coordinator working state without runtime ID as evidence that the model ran.
requirements.rationale: Scheduling/coordination progress differs from runtime acceptance or execution.
requirements.scope: Optional Task path only; ordinary messaging has no Task requirement.

requirements.title: Generate reviewed successor pins from committed blobs
requirements.statement: Preserve the historical P7 pin, commit feature source, generate a separate successor from explicit committed Git blobs, review the manifest/archive/digest and rerun verification before committing pin updates.
requirements.rationale: Updating expected hashes from mutable source defeats provenance checking; root tests alone do not cover dedicated P7 guards.
requirements.scope: P7 source profile, including the current broker-startup catalog. The generic-nats group was removed with the generic-nats code.

requirements.title: Incomplete required groups fail acceptance
requirements.statement: Required acceptance must fail on missing, duplicated, empty, contradictory, failing, skipped, cancelled or timed-out results; timeout remains failure even after exit zero.
requirements.rationale: A harness must not convert absent work or incomplete backends into green product acceptance.
requirements.scope: Current required local P7/native profile; historical permitted skips remain historical evidence only.

The explicit optional shared-group section and adopted group design allow group credential holders to select sibling names/mailboxes; preserve both modes and enforce group boundaries, never promote legacy exclusivity into universal requirement.

conflicts.resolution: Finitev1 trial cleanup is separate from persistentv2 operation. Persistent mode retains intended settings/grants until explicit scoped stop/incident; record mode before invoking cleanup.

Preserve exact resource and route isolation; do not enforce standard-port/exact-/mcp-only globally. Actual ingress interoperability remains unverified.

conflicts.question: Do historical Hermes Runs/Inspector/trial gates become prerequisites of model-free native MCP?
conflicts.resolution: No. Those constraints apply when opting into the fixed execution trial, preserving useful execution safety boundaries. Native transport retains recipient execution/approval and does not add a HAB product runner.

Keep old stage claims as historical evidence; do not make lack of these optional APIs a current invariant. Real product wiring remains unverified. Later the attachment outbox and receiver were deleted with managed attachments; only WriterAdmission remains as an adopted opt-in. The cumulative src/relay/README.md was itself deleted when the durable sender and receiver moved to src/agent-sdk; its successor README describes only the current agent SDK and has no stage claims, so the question is moot.

The attachment receiver's single checkpoint slot was deleted with attachments. Bytes/time/processing/SLO/fleet fairness remain excluded.

conflicts.question: The operations guide said a release rolls back by restarting the earlier build on the same journal and broker store, and the product spec said a code rollback reconciles uncertain requests in the same JetStream journal. The JetStream design says unknown journals are refused and the v1-v3 to v4 migration is one-way, so builds before the JetStream-only release cannot open the schema 4 journal. Which rollback procedure applies?
conflicts.resolution: The backup restore with reconciliation. Since 94e9a0f, OPERATIONS.md allows a same-journal code rollback only to a build that opens the schemas the release wrote (journal schema 4 and agent SDK inbox schema 4); builds up to 3e203d7 refuse a schema 4 journal with journal_key_or_version_mismatch and there is no downgrade migration. Rolling back past that change drains, exports the accepted messages from the schema 4 journal, restores every part of one stopped pre-upgrade backup generation together, and reconciles each exported message by original ID and state before routing traffic; the schema 4 journal copy is kept until then. The product spec section 9, the ADR-016 rollback line and docs/local-relay-service.md now say the same. No requirement statement claimed the same-journal rollback; the claim was in the OPERATIONS.md document summary, which is corrected. HAB-F24 now states the schema bound and the whole-generation restore with original-ID reconciliation. HAB-A07 already forbade lowering schema versions and is unchanged. HAB-D15 and HAB-D16 keep their statements. Since 2b764dd the procedure also reconciles IDs still incomplete in the backup, treats `expired` and `quarantined` as outcome unknown, keeps the earlier build stopped until every restored ID has expired, and settles each ID as delivered, not_saved or unknown from scripts/relay-rollback-reconcile.mjs; HAB-F24 states this. Since 4715b4e the list takes the union of both journals' IDs (a purged incomplete-at-backup ID stays listed), takes `--backup-inbox` and `--execution-record` and lists `restored_bodies` as do_not_process, process or unknown, which a new OPERATIONS.md step 6 settles before each restored recipient restarts; the documents now say the expiry hold stops only redelivery through the relay, not re-execution of a body a restored inbox already holds. HAB-F24 states this. Since the remaining review fixes the root test also drills the restore with the broker store dir, the expiry hold and a recipient restart on the current build; a rollback to the earlier build itself stays a production-operations gate (HAB-C-D04). The local follow-up on 0fc76a6 adds retained recipient evidence to the ID union and an upgraded-only unreleased-body list with application-specific original-key handoff review, since the full restore and wait do not transfer a body first saved after backup. Unknown effects remain stopped and no automatic replay is added.
conflicts.classification: stale operational procedure versus schema version

Native product binding, policy, approval and wake remain manual/unverified.
